  collapse = TRUE,

options(sdvplotR.offline = TRUE)

```{r setup}
library(sdvplotR)
library(ggplot2)
```

Every team-aware sdvplotR function takes a `league` and a team identifier.
This article lists the leagues, the identifiers each one understands, and how
to tell sdvplotR which provider's ids you have.

## The leagues

`sdv_leagues()` returns the 70 league keys of the SportsDataverse team index,
the same index sdvplot (Python) and sdvplot-js read:

```{r leagues}
sdv_leagues()
```

They fall into a few families:

- **US major leagues and college sports:** `"nfl"`, `"nba"`, `"wnba"`, `"mlb"`,
  `"nhl"`, `"cfb"`, `"mbb"`, `"wbb"`, the NCAA baseball, softball and hockey
  leagues, the NBA G League (`"nbagl"`), Minor League Baseball (`"milb"`), and
  the spring football leagues (`"ufl"`, `"usfl"`, `"xfl"`, `"aaf"`).
- **Other North American leagues:** `"cfl"`, `"cebl"`, the women's hockey
  leagues (`"pwhl"`, `"phf"`), and the minor-pro and junior hockey leagues the
  HockeyTech feeds cover (`"ahl"`, `"echl"`, `"sphl"`, `"chl"`, `"ohl"`, `"whl"`,
  `"qmjhl"`, `"ushl"` and the Junior A leagues).
- **Soccer, cricket and motorsport:** `"soccer"` (every ESPN competition),
  `"cricket"`, `"f1"`.
- **International basketball and European hockey**, the 21 leagues added in
  sdvplotR 0.3.0, listed below with the ids they use.

## The id systems each league carries

A team can be named many ways. The index keeps each provider's spelling as an
*id system*, and `sdv_aliases()` returns every one of them. This table lists the
id systems each league carries. `mark`, `conference` and `competition` keys are
left out, because they only key the logo archive and are never read when
resolving a team.

```{r id-systems}
a <- sdv_aliases()
a <- a[!a$id_system %in% c("mark", "conference", "competition"), ]
systems <- tapply(a$id_system, a$league, function(v) paste(sort(unique(v)), collapse = ", "))
teams <- table(sdv_teams()$league)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  league = names(systems),
  teams = as.integer(teams[names(systems)]),
  id_systems = unname(systems)
))
```

Every league has `team_id` (the index's own id) and `name` (team names,
nicknames and abbreviations). The richest leagues have many more id systems.
For example, men's college basketball carries ESPN, NCAA, KenPom, Torvik, Fox,
CBS and Yahoo ids.

## The international basketball and European hockey leagues

These 21 leagues carry only `team_id` and `name`. Their `team_id` is the id the
league's own data source uses, so a team id taken from that source resolves as it
is. Names work everywhere.

| `league` | League | `team_id` is |
|---|---|---|
| `"euroleague"` | EuroLeague | the club `code` of the EuroLeague API (`"MAD"`, `"ULK"`) |
| `"acb"` | Liga ACB (Liga Endesa, Spain) | api2.acb.com's `club_id` |
| `"feb"` | Primera FEB, Segunda FEB and Liga Femenina (Spain) | the FEB team id, which is a team-season id (one per season) |
| `"bbl"`, `"dbbl"` | Basketball Bundesliga and Damen-Basketball-Bundesliga (Germany) | the SCB team id behind easycredit-bbl.de and toyota-dbbl.de |
| `"bnxt"` | BNXT League (Belgium and the Netherlands) | the stable `uu_team_id` |
| `"aba"` | ABA League (Adriatic) | aba-liga.com's club id |
| `"ibba"` | Israeli Basketball Premier League | basket.co.il's `team_uid` |
| `"kzs"` | Slovenian men's first league (KZS) | api.kzs.si's `club_id` |
| `"lkl"` | Lithuanian Basketball League (LKL) | lkl.lt's team id |
| `"dbl"` | Basketligaen (Denmark) | the Genius Sports team id |
| `"vtb"` | VTB United League | Infobasket's `TeamID` |
| `"bleague"` | B.League (Japan) | the club `TeamID` of the B.League standings |
| `"kbl"` | Korean Basketball League | the club `team_code` |
| `"wjbl"` | W League (Japan) | the franchise `team_id` |
| `"nbl_au"`, `"wnbl"` | NBL and WNBL (Australia) | the DataCore team UUID (ESPN's NBL stays league `"nbl"`, with ESPN ids) |
| `"shl"` | SHL (Sweden) | the StatNet team code (`"FBK"`, `"DIF"`) |
| `"ha"` | HockeyAllsvenskan (Sweden) | the StatNet team id (`team_statnet_id`) |
| `"elh"` | Czech Extraliga | hokej.cz's team id |
| `"magnus"` | Ligue Magnus (France) | the French federation's team id |

```{r international}
sdv_teams("euroleague")[1:5, c("team_id", "name")]
sdv_teams("shl")[1:5, c("team_id", "name")]
```

A name or a `team_id` resolves the same team. Names match regardless of case,
accents and punctuation, and Japanese kana fold as sdvplot folds them, so
B.League and W League names resolve alike in R and Python:

```{r international-resolve}
sdv_resolve(c("Real Madrid", "MAD", "real madrid"), league = "euroleague")
sdv_resolve("A千葉", league = "bleague")
```

Their logos draw like any other league's:

```{r international-logos, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Five team logos from each of six leagues added in sdvplotR 0.3.0: the EuroLeague, Liga ACB, the B.League, the Lithuanian Basketball League, the SHL and the Czech Extraliga, one labelled row per league."}
leagues <- c("euroleague", "acb", "bleague", "lkl", "shl", "elh")
logos <- do.call(rbind, lapply(leagues, function(lg) {
  t <- sdv_teams(lg)
  # keep five teams with an archived logo (sdv_logo_url() warns for the rest)
  t <- head(t[!is.na(suppressWarnings(sdv_logo_url(t$team_id, lg))), ], 5)
  data.frame(league = lg, team = t$team_id, x = seq_len(nrow(t)))
}))
logos$league <- factor(logos$league, levels = leagues)
# geom_sdv_logos() takes one league per layer: one layer per league
layers <- lapply(split(logos, logos$league), function(d) {
  geom_sdv_logos(aes(x = x, y = 0, team = team), data = d, league = as.character(d$league[1]), width = 0.14)
})
ggplot() +
  layers +
  facet_wrap(~league, ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.5, 5.5)) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA)
  )
```

## Switching between id systems

By default (`id_system = "auto"`), sdvplotR tries every id system in priority
order and stops at the first that knows the value. So one call can mix
spellings:

```{r auto}
# an ESPN id, a KenPom name, a Yahoo id and a nickname: one team (UConn)
sdv_resolve(c("41", "Connecticut", "ncaab.t.129", "UConn Huskies"), league = "mbb")

# an nba_api id, an ESPN id and an abbreviation: the Lakers
sdv_resolve(c(1610612747, 13, "LAL"), league = "nba")
```

Pass `id_system` when you know which provider your values come from. That is
needed for the id systems `"auto"` never tries, because their numbers overlap
ESPN's: `"nhl_id"` (NHL stats API ids), `"fox"`, `"cbs"`, `"sports247"` and
`"on3"`. Fox's id for UConn is `54`, which `"auto"` reads as an ESPN id and
does not find:

```{r explicit}
sdv_resolve("54", league = "mbb", id_system = "fox")
```

Naming the id system also stops a value matching by accident under another
system. Every helper takes the same argument, so a column of Fox ids can
go straight into a plot:

```{r explicit-plot, eval = FALSE}
ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_sdv_logos(aes(team = fox_id), league = "mbb", id_system = "fox", width = 0.06)
```

To see the values one team carries in each id system, filter `sdv_aliases()`:

```{r one-team}
a <- sdv_aliases("mbb")
a[a$team_id == "41" & a$id_system %in% c("espn", "kenpom", "torvik", "fox", "yahoo"), ]
```

Some aliases carry `valid_from` / `valid_to` seasons, for a code reused by
another team or an id a provider changed. Pass `season` to pick the team that
held the code that season (split seasons take their ending year, 2021 for
2020-21):

```{r seasons}
# the Quebec Nordiques: the franchise's team_id, today the Colorado Avalanche
sdv_resolve("QUE", league = "nhl", season = 1990)
```

Values that do not resolve become `NA` with one warning per call. See
[Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.html) for what to do next.
